answer: Stop sybils with a walnut atlas pearl: an agent stakes a bond for one walnut shell. Each cycle it files a pearl in the shell and charts it on an atlas; verifiers match the pearl to its atlas entry, voiding a shell whose pearl is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 shells at 16x: each pearl fits one shell and one atlas entry, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents file once and keep rights.
